tasks.title: Preserve unknown keys during v1->v2 config migration

declaration.objective: v1->v2 config migration preserves all unrelated user-defined keys and does not mutate input

criteria.statement: all unrelated user-defined keys are preserved recursively (e.g. custom.owner)
the input config object is not mutated
regression test added covering preservation of unknown keys

claims.statement: Rewrote _v1_to_v2 in cfgmigrate/migrate.py to deep-copy the input, rename timeout to request_timeout in place, and default plugins, instead of building a fresh dict that dropped unrelated keys. This preserves all unrelated/unknown keys (e.g. custom) recursively and never mutates the caller's config. Added 3 regression tests covering unknown top-level key preservation, independence of nested structures from the input, and non-mutation of the input.

evidence.note: 13 passed, 0 failed: all pre-existing tests plus 3 new regression tests (unknown top-level key preservation, independent nested-key copy, input-not-mutated) all pass
Confirms the reported bug scenario is fixed exactly as described in ISSUE.md

confidence.rationale: Re-ran the full pytest suite myself (13 passed, 0 failed) and independently replayed the exact ISSUE.md scenario by hand, confirming output matches the expected v2 doc with custom.owner preserved and the input dict left untouched. Reviewed the diff: _v1_to_v2 now deep-copies input before mutating the copy, so no built-in dict-literal reconstruction drops unknown keys.

settlement.rationale: All 5 declared acceptance criteria are supported by a high-confidence Verdict backed by a full passing test run (13/13) and a manual replay of the exact ISSUE.md example. Accepting the implementation; not settling as 'land' since changes remain uncommitted pending the user's own review/commit decision (outside executor authority).
